title: Two-Step Word Problems
introduction: Build on Primary 1 knowledge and practise two-step word problems.
definition: A two-step problem requires more than one operation. Identify the quantities, plan the order of operations, calculate one step at a time and check the result against the situation.

examples.question: A shop has 120 pencils, receives 48 more and sells 35.
Four boxes have 8 pencils each. Six pencils are removed.

exercises.question: A farmer has 150 eggs, collects 75 more and sells 60. Remaining?
Five bags have 6 sweets each. 4 sweets are eaten. Remaining?
24 books are shared among 4 pupils. Each gets 2 more. Books per pupil?
You have RM20, spend RM7 and receive RM5. Remaining RM?
Three containers each hold 2 L. Pour out 1 L. Remaining litres?
A bus has 35 passengers. 12 leave and 9 board. Total?

summary: A two-step problem requires more than one operation. Identify the quantities, plan the order of operations, calculate one step at a time and check the result against the situation.
